title: Operator Credential Boundary and Key Escrow Onboarding Protocol
creator: Elena Martinez
description: This PRD defines the operational and compliance requirements for onboarding enterprise customers to Private deployments where operator credentials and customer key lifecycle interact. The doc prescribes the boundary between operator access and customer-managed key custody, the escrow/escrowless options, audit artifact requirements, SSO/SAML federation patterns, RBAC role mappings, and explicit acceptance criteria for signoff. Aim: create a repeatable, auditable onboarding protocol that satisfies SOC/ISO auditors and enterprise security teams while minimizing friction for customers.
background: Multiple recent enterprise customers requested guarantees around operator separation of duties, key custody, and verifiable audit trails for Private deployments (VPC and on-prem). Previous artifacts are fragmented across playbooks. This protocol consolidates decisions and artifacts required for a green onboarding, including proof points for SSO assertions, RBAC policies, KMS/HSM integration, and key escrow or customer-held options.
objectives: Define clear operator access boundaries for support and upgrade operations
Standardize SSO/SAML federation patterns and mapping expectations
Specify KMS/HSM integration modes and required evidence for customer onboarding
Provide a minimal set of audit artifacts and retention guarantees for compliance
Create a phased acceptance and signoff checklist to streamline security reviews
success_metrics: Time from customer onboarding request to security signoff <= 10 business days
100% of onboarded customers have automated audit evidence uploaded to retention storage
No post-onboarding high-severity access control incidents within first 90 days
Operator access requests during onboarding documented and approved with ticket traces
scope: In-scope: Private deployment onboarding (VPC and on-prem) for customers requiring SSO/SAML, RBAC, and KMS/HSM integration. Includes operator support flows, key escrow options, evidence package requirements, playbook templates, and tests required for acceptance. Out-of-scope: Hosted API customers and non-production evaluation clusters.
out_of_scope: Development-only environments and ephemeral test clusters
acceptance_criteria: SSO/SAML: Successful end-to-end SAML federation test with customer IdP including signature verification and assertion attribute mapping (subject, email, roles)
RBAC: Role mapping documented and enforced; at least two RBAC roles validated (customer-admin, customer-operator) with least-privilege checks
KMS/HSM: Customer keys integrated via configured KMS connector. For customer-managed keys, a verification transaction using a signed ciphertext must succeed
Key Rotation: Rotation workflow executed in staging with successful decryption of existing ciphertext and verification in logs
Audit logs: Immutable audit trail for operator actions enabled, retention configured >= 1 year, and a sample export demonstrates non-repudiation evidence
Operator Boundary: Support access requires time-bound, ticket-linked escalation with MFA and just-in-time elevation; at least one test escalation performed and recorded
Evidence Package: Consolidated evidence (SAML metadata, RBAC mapping file, KMS connector config, rotation test artifacts, log exports, runbook) uploaded to secure evidence bucket and linked in ticket
Security Review: Security team completes checklist and records signoff in the ticket thread

test_plan: SAML end-to-end: IdP -> SP SAML handshake, signed assertions validated, expired assertion rejected
RBAC enforcement: Attempt unauthorized action as operator role and confirm deny; confirm allowed actions for customer-admin
KMS flow: Encrypt with customer key, decrypt via service pipeline, verify logs reflect key id and operation
Rotation test: Rotate key in staging, re-encrypt sample blob, validate continuity of service
Audit tamper test: Export logs, compute hash, attempt simulated tamper and verify detection via checksum
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Runbook and tests validated in internal staging cluster (2 weeks). Phase 2: Select pilot customer (1 customer) for full onboarding with Security present (3 weeks). Phase 3: Iterate on pilot feedback, update playbook, enable as standard onboarding path. Each phase requires signoff on the checklist items before moving to the next.
rollback_criteria: If any high-severity cryptographic failure occurs during KMS integration testing
If SAML assertions cannot be validated reproducibly across supported IdPs
If immutable audit evidence cannot be produced or hash verification fails
If operator boundary tests show privilege escalation beyond documented limits
risks: Customer IdP incompatibilities causing repeated integration cycles
KMS vendor HSM constraints preventing certain rotation flows
Operational friction for customers choosing escrow vs customer-held keys
Audit evidence storage and retention cost pushback from Finance
mitigations: Maintain SAML test harness covering common IdPs (Okta, AzureAD, ADFS) and document attribute mappings
Support two KMS integration modes: connector-based and proxy-bridged to accommodate HSM quirks
Offer a decision template mapping pros/cons of escrow models and recommended default
Estimate evidence storage costs and include in onboarding fee or reserved capacity contract
